page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the top 25% at 2693.38. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the middle 50%, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 21558.27 and a PassMark CPU score of 22027.2. Memory bandwidth is moderate, delivering 1018.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Other operations, including static web serving throughput at 15.62 GB/sec and LLM inference speed for a small 135M model, consistently register in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 is its highly constrained memory allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. However, this resource density provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX capabilities. This hardware profile is suited for workloads such as software compilation, web serving, text processing, and lightweight CPU-based inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 8 physical cores. This configuration lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng score of 2693.38, while multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and web serving throughput align with average mid-tier standards. The instance supports cryptographic and integer instruction sets like AES and SHA_NI, but lacks AVX-512. Given its high vCPU count relative to memory, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy, memory-light workloads such as software compilation, web serving, and basic text processing.
